name: Arcuate ligament
description: Inconstant Y-shaped thickening of the posterolateral capsule from the fibular styloid apex, its medial limb arching over the popliteus musculotendinous junction. When visible, a thin low-signal band behind the popliteus tendon on coronal oblique or posterior coronal images.
variants_pitfalls: Often absent or invisible (cadavers 24–100%; MRI 10–46% depending on technique): not seeing it is normal.
With a large fabella expect a thick fabellofibular ligament and a small or absent arcuate ligament. The fabella (about 25–37% of knees) is a sesamoid, not a loose body.

Arcuate sign: a small horizontal styloid tip avulsion marks a posterolateral corner injury; in one small series all 13 knees also had a PCL injury, so check the PCL. Styloid edema without a fragment may be the only sign.

Injury to the ligament itself is rarely seen on MRI (in one series none of the 6 disruptions found among 10 knees explored was seen on MRI), so judge the corner by the LCL, popliteus tendon, popliteofibular ligament and styloid. Fluid behind the popliteus tendon outside the recess suggests a capsular tear.
